title: A Drop for the Protocol
premise: August Nystrom, an analyst discarded by three agencies for asking the wrong questions, is hired off-books to investigate a passenger flight whose records evaporate mid-flight — while the plane is still airborne. The trail leads to the Protocol, a covert network that grooms and burns analysts like August, and to an inheritance: a dead mentor's encrypted ledger naming everyone the Protocol owns. As a global summit approaches, where the Protocol plans to detonate its final asset, August must choose between exposing the truth and surviving it. In the end, August burns the network from inside its own archive, trades their last shred of anonymity for the ledger's release, and walks away belonging to no one but themselves.
about_author: Wendell Montrose is a former intelligence archivist who spent eleven years cataloguing things governments preferred forgotten before turning to fiction. He writes from a coastal town he refuses to name, and claims every thriller is a memoir with the serial numbers filed off.

chapters.title: The Unattributable Man
chapters.summary: August Nystrom, POV. Fired from three agencies, August takes ghost work — cases no firm will sign. A fixer named Corvane offers a retainer too clean to trust: find out why flight KX-409 has no record while it's still in the air. The beat is weary competence masking hunger for belonging.

chapters.title: Forty Minutes of Nothing
chapters.summary: August, POV. Cross-referencing radar archives, air traffic logs, and a hobbyist tracker's screenshots, August confirms the impossible: forty minutes of KX-409's flight path exist only in fragments. One fragment shows the plane deviating toward a closed military corridor. Beat: the thrill of being needed again, sharpened by dread.

chapters.title: Landing Without a Shadow
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: August and Ilse Brandt, a flight attendant on KX-409 who landed, walked off the tarmac, and found her employment history erased by morning. Ilse remembers a passenger in seat 14C who never deplaned. Beat: two strangers realizing they've been edited out of reality.

chapters.title: The Mentor's Bequest
chapters.summary: August, POV. A solicitor delivers a posthumous package from Halvard Reyes, August's first handler, dead six weeks. Inside: a key fob and a note reading 'the training was the product.' August recognizes the phrasing from their own recruitment years ago. Beat: grief curdling into suspicion that Halvard was murdered.

chapters.title: Seat 14C
chapters.summary: Ilse, POV. Hiding in a Rotterdam safehouse, Ilse reconstructs the vanished passenger from memory — a man with institutional posture and a government-issue watch. She emails August through a dead-drop address Halvard once gave her. Beat: fear becoming agency; the erased choosing to testify.

chapters.title: The Fob Opens a Door
chapters.summary: August, POV. The fob unlocks a storage unit in Malmö containing Halvard's partial ledger — encrypted pages naming analysts, handlers, and one recurring word: PROTOCOL. Also a photograph of August's own induction class, three faces already dead. Beat: inheritance as indictment; August learns they were built, not hired.

chapters.title: Corvane's Real Client
chapters.summary: August, POV. Following money trails, August discovers Corvane's retainer originates from a shell tied to the summit's host committee — someone inside wants the Protocol exposed, or wants August as bait. Confronting Corvane yields a half-truth and a warning. Beat: paranoia; every ally now suspect.

chapters.title: What They Trained Into You
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, August's POV. Interleaved with present-day decryption, August recalls their recruitment: aptitude tests disguised as therapy, loyalty framed as family, the slow teaching that survival means compliance. Present-day August realizes the Protocol still has hooks in them. Beat: the horror of loving something designed to use you.

chapters.title: Nine Days to the Summit
chapters.summary: Dual POV: August and Ilse converge in Geneva, where the Global Aviation Compact convenes in nine days. The ledger's decrypted fragments reference 'the drop' — an event scheduled to coincide with the summit. Beat: urgency compressing the investigation into a countdown.

chapters.title: The Archive Beneath the Lake
chapters.summary: August, POV. Halvard's notes point to a decommissioned data vault under Lake Geneva holding the Protocol's full records. August and Ilse scout it and find it active, guarded by contractors wearing no insignia. Beat: awe at the scale of the machine, and the first taste of real danger.

chapters.title: A Name That Buys Silence
chapters.summary: Ilse, POV. Ilse identifies seat 14C: Dr. Emil Varga, a Protocol architect presumed dead in 2019 — meaning his appearance on KX-409 was either resurrection or defection. Her discovery gets her safehouse burned; she escapes by minutes. Beat: knowledge as liability; the cost of looking closer.

chapters.title: Handlers and Ghosts
chapters.summary: August, POV. August tracks down Sable, a fellow inductee turned Protocol enforcer, and bargains for Varga's location. Sable reveals the Protocol's endgame: 'the drop' will release fabricated evidence collapsing three governments on summit day, and the Protocol inherits the wreckage. Beat: recognition between two products of the same machine.

chapters.title: The Price Quoted in Blood
chapters.summary: August, POV. Sable offers August reinstatement — belonging, purpose, protection — if they hand over the ledger. August stalls, understanding the offer is both genuine and a trap. That night, Corvane is found drowned. Beat: temptation at its most seductive; the price of survival made explicit.

chapters.title: Six Days
chapters.summary: August and Ilse, alternating POV. With Corvane dead and Sable's leash tightening, the pair go dark, decrypting the ledger in a moving caravan across the Alps. They learn Varga is alive inside the lake vault, kept as insurance against the Protocol's own operatives. Beat: fugitive intimacy; trust forged under pressure.

chapters.title: Varga's Confession
chapters.summary: August, POV. Posing as a Protocol auditor, August reaches Varga, who confesses he faked his death to build a kill-switch into the drop mechanism — but needs the ledger's master key to arm it. He gives August the vault's maintenance schedule. Beat: hope arriving wrapped in manipulation; can a liar's confession be believed?

chapters.title: Sable Closes the Circle
chapters.summary: Ilse, POV. Sable corners Ilse, offering her old life back in exchange for August's location. Ilse feeds him false coordinates, buying hours, then goes to warn August — and finds the caravan already surrounded. Beat: loyalty tested past reason; sacrifice without applause.

chapters.title: Into the Vault
chapters.summary: August, POV. Using the maintenance window, August infiltrates the lake vault during a Protocol drill, finds the archive intact, and begins arming Varga's kill-switch. Alarms trip early — Sable anticipated the schedule. Beat: claustrophobic tension; the inheritance within reach as the trap springs.

chapters.title: The Drop Begins
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. Two days before the summit, the Protocol initiates the drop early: fabricated dossiers begin flooding media channels, markets wobble, and the summit's security apparatus turns inward hunting ghosts. August, trapped in the vault, must finish the kill-switch mid-crisis. Beat: the world tilting; personal stakes swallowed by global ones.

chapters.title: Burn the Network
chapters.summary: August, POV. Climax part one: August triggers the kill-switch, cascading deletions through the Protocol's archive, then broadcasts the true ledger to every delegate's terminal at the summit. Sable confronts August in the vault; their fight ends with Sable choosing, at the last second, not to pull the trigger. Beat: catharsis through fire; betrayal answered with exposure, not vengeance.

chapters.title: What Survives the Fire
chapters.summary: Ilse, POV. The summit fractures as delegates scramble; the Protocol's surviving principals scatter or surrender. Ilse testifies publicly, reclaiming her name and the names of the lost, including seat 14C. Varga vanishes into the chaos, his motives forever ambiguous. Beat: mourning and vindication entwined; some truths cost more than lies.

chapters.title: No Attribution Required
chapters.summary: August, POV. Agencies circle, offering rehabilitation in exchange for silence about what the ledger revealed about their own complicity. August declines all of them, releasing the remaining unredacted pages openly. Beat: refusal as rebirth; belonging finally chosen over granted.

chapters.title: A Drop of Clear Water
chapters.summary: August, POV, epilogue. Months later, August lives unlisted in a town that doesn't ask questions, meeting Ilse once a year by tradition. A letter arrives bearing Halvard's handwriting — dated after his death. August reads it, smiles, and burns it. Beat: quiet resolution with one unresolved thread; survival, at last, on their own terms.
